OLYMPUS SITE RELAY FEED V1
Revised contract draft for review
2026-10-29

STATUS

This document is a design contract, not a production activation notice. It supersedes the
2026-10-27 feed proposal. No endpoint, credential, parser or relay-to-site adapter is represented
as live by this document.

The words REQUIRED, PROPOSED and OPEN DECISION have precise meanings here:

- REQUIRED records a direction already established in the review.
- PROPOSED is the current implementation recommendation and still needs explicit agreement.
- OPEN DECISION must be frozen before fixtures become an executable contract.

The deliberate manual .198 export remains unchanged. It keeps its own file, parser, storage
candidate, consent flow and expiry rules. The relay feed described here is a separate endpoint,
schema and candidate. Army QR and Olympus Link remain on their separate gates and receive no
authority or activation from this feed.


1. PURPOSE AND TRUST STATEMENT

REQUIRED: The feed publishes bounded, masked observations of native in-game guild rosters. It is
not proof of membership, verification, a unique human, a Discord identity or Council authority.

REQUIRED: A published metric needs a quorum of distinct qualifying, deduplicated linked-account
witnesses. This wording is deliberate. Multiple accounts or characters can still belong to one
human. The system must never describe its result as deduplicated or verified unique people.

REQUIRED: Single-source, conflicting, expired, revoked, deleted or withdrawn results expose a
state and bounded source time only. They expose no count, leading value, witness total or conflict
partition.


2. POLLING ENDPOINT

PROPOSED endpoint:

  GET https://<relay-host>/companion/v1/site/aggregates?v=1&scope=forever-pve-alliance
  Authorization: Bearer <compact-JWS>
  If-None-Match: "<previous-strong-etag>"

REQUIRED:

- The website polls every five minutes. Push and ping remain out of v1.
- The route is read-only and server-to-server. The credential never reaches browser code.
- Sign-in, Companion-session and Olympus Link credentials are refused on this route.
- The endpoint returns one complete atomic snapshot for one canonical scope.
- A missing or malformed required guild row invalidates the entire response. It never means
  "keep the previous value".

PROPOSED operational limit: 30 requests per minute per feed credential, followed by HTTP 429 and
Retry-After. This limit is not a source of individual, member or Council authority.

OPEN DECISION: Confirm the endpoint path above. Once frozen, the exact origin, path and canonical
query serialization become part of the signed request target.


3. FEED-REQUEST JWS

REQUIRED: The website signs a short-lived compact JWS with a dedicated Ed25519 feed-request key.
The key is separate from Discord sign-in, Companion sessions, Olympus Link and every Council or
member key. The private key stays server-side and is never logged.

Protected header:

  {
    "alg": "EdDSA",
    "kid": "<feed-key-id>",
    "typ": "olympus-feed-request+jwt"
  }

Claims:

  {
    "v": 1,
    "iss": "olympus-site",
    "aud": "olympus-site-aggregates",
    "iat": 1800000000,
    "exp": 1800000060,
    "jti": "<at-least-128-bits-of-randomness>",
    "htm": "GET",
    "htu": "https://<relay-host>/companion/v1/site/aggregates?v=1&scope=forever-pve-alliance",
    "scope": "forever-pve-alliance"
  }

REQUIRED validation:

- Pin alg to EdDSA. Never use an algorithm named only by the untrusted token.
- Resolve kid only against the dedicated feed-request allowlist. Two explicitly configured keys
  may overlap during rotation.
- Require the protected typ value to equal olympus-feed-request+jwt exactly.
- Require the signed claim v to equal integer 1 exactly.
- Pin iss and aud to the exact configured values.
- Require integer iat and exp, exp greater than iat, and exp - iat no greater than 60 seconds.
- At validation time now, reject the request when iat > now + clockSkew or
  now > exp + clockSkew. A token that is structurally well formed is not valid before its
  permitted iat window or after its permitted exp window.
- Bind htm to GET, htu to the exact canonical HTTPS endpoint and query, and scope to the requested
  canonical scope.
- Atomically consume each jti once across every relay instance. Retain the replay record until
  after exp plus the accepted clock-skew window.
- Redact Authorization, the compact JWS, jti and all key material from application, proxy, error
  and analytics logs.
- A valid polling credential identifies only the website. It grants and asserts no individual
  Council, member, contributor or verification authority.

PROPOSED maximum clock skew: five seconds in either direction.


4. CANONICAL SCOPE

REQUIRED logical scope:

  id: forever-pve-alliance
  faction: Alliance
  guilds, in this exact canonical order:
    Olympus
    Olympus I
    Olympus II
    Olympus III
    Olympus IV
    Olympus V
    Olympus VI
    Olympus VII
    Olympus VIII
    Olympus IX
    Olympus X

REQUIRED:

- The relay maps its exact native realm-group value to this logical scope server-side.
- Client-provided aliases, free-form realm combinations such as RealmA+RealmB, other factions and
  all other guild names are rejected rather than normalized into this scope.
- A scope-mapping change increments mappingVersion and requires a reviewed fixture update.

OPEN DECISION: Record the exact canonical Forever PvE realm-group value and the minimal accepted
native aliases. Do not activate the endpoint with a placeholder mapping.


5. QUALIFYING CONTRIBUTORS AND DEDUPLICATION

REQUIRED:

- Multiple devices and characters linked to one account count as one witness for a guild and
  metric.
- The relay deduplicates before aggregation and keeps only the newest eligible observation for
  each deduplicated witness and metric.
- The same uploaded checkpoint cannot count twice.
- An unverified character claim cannot force two accounts to merge.
- A merge can only preserve or lower the number of eligible witnesses; it cannot manufacture a
  new witness.
- A roster observation for guild G qualifies only when it is the contributor's native own-roster
  observation for G. Relayed, second-hand, seen-only and disputed rows do not qualify.
- characters means roster characters, including alts. It is not a unique-player estimate.

PROPOSED safer v1 rule: only an authenticated account with an established linked-account identity
is a qualifying witness. An unverified character claim may be held as non-qualifying evidence but
does not count toward quorum until linked.

OPEN DECISION: Confirm whether any authenticated but unverified account may count. If the answer
is yes, define its separate risk class and show that it cannot be multiplied or used to force an
account merge.

PROPOSED privacy implementation: use a relay-generated opaque internal contributor identifier or
a per-person deletable salt. Do not expose it. Do not use a globally reproducible public hash that
can recreate a contributor after erasure.


6. COUNCIL WITNESS DESIGNATION

REQUIRED:

- Council designation is independent authority metadata on the relay.
- A Council witness counts once, exactly like another qualifying witness.
- Council status cannot replace the two-witness quorum, break a tie, override a conflict, choose a
  cluster, widen a scope, grant feed access or alter a count.
- No public feed field reveals whether a Council witness participated.
- Expiring or revoking Council designation removes only the designation. The contributor may still
  count as an ordinary qualifying witness unless their contributor eligibility is separately
  revoked.

PROPOSED authoritative source: the current signed HS1 Council membership source. HT1 titles alone
must not create Council membership.

OPEN DECISION: Confirm the authoritative Council source, its owner, refresh cadence, expiry and
revocation procedure.


7. ELIGIBLE OBSERVATIONS AND TIME

REQUIRED:

- Character totals and online counts are aggregated independently.
- Character quorum never supplies online quorum.
- Online needs at least two sufficiently fresh, independently agreeing observations of its own.
- Online zero is a valid exact observation and must not be converted to missing.
- Count masking occurs after aggregation, never before cluster selection.

PROPOSED freshness windows:

  characters: 1,800 seconds
  online:       900 seconds

REQUIRED timestamp model:

- An exact source timestamp t is the interval [t,t].
- A source timestamp explicitly rounded down to five minutes is [t,t+299].
- Interval A is definitely newer than B only when A.notBefore > B.notAfter.
- Overlapping intervals are a tie; neither source is strictly newer.
- Reject impossible interval order, excessive width and a notBefore value beyond the configured
  future-skew allowance. A rounded interval may end slightly after receipt only because of its
  declared rounding window.
- Freshness uses the oldest plausible time, notBefore.
- Every observation in an accepted cluster must satisfy the metric's freshness window.
- The aggregate expires at the earliest participating notBefore plus the freshness window.

For an accepted metric, sourceTime is one bounded coarse source bucket, never a span across all
participating observations:

- Select the accepted observation with the earliest notBefore.
- If more than one has that notBefore, select the one with the earliest notAfter, then the lowest
  opaque internal witness identifier only as a deterministic private tie-breaker.
- Publish exactly that selected observation's interval as sourceTime.
- sourceTime.notAfter - sourceTime.notBefore must be between 0 and 299 seconds.
- validUntil is sourceTime.notBefore plus the metric freshness window.

This oldest-participating-bucket rule is conservative for expiry and does not reveal the temporal
dispersion of the witness set. Example: accepted observations from [1800001200,1800001499] and
[1800001500,1800001500] publish sourceTime [1800001200,1800001499], not the wider interval
[1800001200,1800001500]. Character validUntil is then 1800003000 under the proposed 1,800-second
window.

For a nonaccepted state, expose only one bounded sourceTime bucket for the most recent eligible
observation, using the inverse deterministic ordering. It is informational, never wider than 299
seconds, and carries no count or partition.

The site derives displayed age from the original sourceTime interval. HTTP response time, poll time,
cache time and a 304 response never become a new source time.


8. DETERMINISTIC AGREEMENT

For each guild and metric:

1. Select the newest eligible observation for each already-deduplicated qualifying witness.
2. Let N be all eligible deduplicated witnesses for that metric, including outliers. N is the
   majority denominator and never appears in the public response.
3. Sort observations by numeric value and then by the opaque internal witness identifier.
4. Define direct agreement as:

     abs(a-b) <= max(absoluteTolerance, ceil(relativeTolerance * max(a,b)))

5. Enumerate maximal contiguous clusters whose minimum and maximum directly agree. Do not join an
   A-B-C chain merely because A agrees with B and B agrees with C.
6. Deduplicate clusters with identical membership.
7. Accept only one unique largest cluster that contains at least two witnesses and satisfies:

     clusterSize / N > 0.5

8. Equal largest clusters are conflict, including overlapping equal clusters in a nontransitive
   chain.
9. Publish the deterministic median of the accepted cluster.
10. precision is exact only when every accepted value is identical. If tolerance joined different
    values, precision is approximate.

Consequences required by this rule:

- Four agreeing values and one outlier are accepted: 4/5 is an 80 percent majority. The earlier
  Olympus II no-majority example was incorrect.
- Two agreeing values and one outlier are accepted.
- Two values against two values are conflict.
- A nontransitive chain with two equal largest directly compatible clusters is conflict.
- A single source is no-quorum and exposes no value.

PROPOSED tolerances:

  characters: absoluteTolerance 5, relativeTolerance 0.05
  online:     absoluteTolerance 2, relativeTolerance 0.05

OPEN DECISION: Freeze the median for an even accepted cluster before fixtures become normative:

- Option A, recommended for a symmetric estimate: floor((lowerMiddle + upperMiddle + 1) / 2).
- Option B, compatible with the older draft: lowerMiddle.

The choice must be a schema policy constant and cannot vary by guild or request.

For reproducible illustration only, the examples and fixtures in this review package
provisionally use Option A, the rounded middle-pair median. This is a fixture assumption,
not a record of final agreement or production behavior.
The reference examples and fixtures provisionally use Option A so they can remain deterministic;
that fixture choice does not close the OPEN DECISION or authorize production behavior.

Online runs the same algorithm over its own fresh eligible observations. PROPOSED privacy gate:
online may be published only when characters is also accepted, solely so complementary masking
can be evaluated. This does not allow character quorum to substitute for online quorum.


9. MASKING AFTER AGGREGATION

REQUIRED masking, aligned with the deliberate manual export:

- A positive accepted count from one through four is published only as the nonnumeric band few.
- Online zero remains the exact numeric value zero.
- If the character total is hidden, online is unavailable.
- If an exact online value would reveal an offline remainder from one through four, online is
  unavailable with reason complementary-small-group.
- Witness totals, Council participation, agreeing/disagreeing totals, conflict groups, partitions,
  raw values, contributor identifiers, hashes and claims are never public, even when the guild
  count itself is large.


10. EXACT RESPONSE SCHEMA

The v1 parser is exact. Unknown or missing keys reject the entire response. A change to key shape
requires v2.

Top level:

  {
    "schema": "olympus-site-relay-feed",
    "version": 1,
    "producer": "olympus-relay/site.1",
    "sequence": 42,
    "generatedAt": 1800001800,
    "complete": true,
    "scope": {
      "id": "forever-pve-alliance",
      "mappingVersion": 1,
      "faction": "Alliance"
    },
    "guilds": [ exactly eleven canonical rows ]
  }

generatedAt is the material snapshot creation time. It changes only when sequence changes; it is
not rewritten on every HTTP response.

Each guild row:

  {
    "guild": "Olympus II",
    "source": "companion-relay",
    "basis": "own-roster",
    "characters": <metric-result>,
    "online": <metric-result>
  }

Available exact or approximate metric:

  {
    "status": "available",
    "value": 987,
    "precision": "approximate",
    "sourceTime": { "notBefore": 1800000000, "notAfter": 1800000299 },
    "validUntil": 1800001800
  }

Small accepted metric:

  {
    "status": "masked",
    "band": "few",
    "precision": "exact",
    "sourceTime": { "notBefore": 1800000000, "notAfter": 1800000299 },
    "validUntil": 1800001800
  }

Unavailable metric:

  {
    "status": "unavailable",
    "reason": "conflict",
    "sourceTime": { "notBefore": 1800000000, "notAfter": 1800000299 }
  }

Allowed unavailable reasons:

  not-observed
  no-quorum
  no-fresh-quorum
  conflict
  expired
  revoked
  deleted
  withdrawn
  complementary-small-group

For not-observed, sourceTime is null. No unavailable result has value, band, precision or
validUntil.
No row contains a label, corroboratedBy, contributors or conflict object. The website maps bounded
state codes to its own display copy.


11. COMPLETE SNAPSHOTS, WITHDRAWAL AND TOMBSTONES

REQUIRED:

- Every HTTP 200 response contains exactly the eleven canonical guild rows.
- deleted, revoked, withdrawn and not-observed rows are explicit tombstone states inside the
  complete snapshot. A row is never silently omitted.
- The consumer atomically accepts or rejects the entire snapshot.
- A previously accepted relay value is withdrawn when it loses quorum, conflicts, expires, is
  revoked, is deleted or disappears from the relay's complete source set.
- A revocation or deletion removes the affected observation, recomputes the metric and invalidates
  the prior snapshot. If the remaining observations still form quorum, a new accepted result may
  be emitted under a new sequence and ETag.
- Network failure never extends validUntil. After expiry, relay data is unavailable even if an old
  response remains cached.


12. SEQUENCE, ETAG AND HTTP 304

REQUIRED:

- sequence is monotonic per canonical scope.
- sequence changes on every material value or state transition, including acceptance, masking,
  loss of quorum, conflict, expiry, revocation, deletion, withdrawal and a changed sourceTime.
- The strong ETag is derived from the canonical response bytes for the current sequence.
- Aging that crosses a freshness or validity boundary is a material transition and must produce a
  new sequence/ETag even if no new observation arrived.
- A matching If-None-Match returns HTTP 304 only while the evaluated material snapshot is still
  identical.
- A 304 has no feed body and never updates sourceTime, validUntil, sequence, manual timestamp,
  cache acquisition time used for freshness or any candidate age.

The HTTP Date header may reflect response time. It is never a source timestamp.


13. MANUAL EXPORT COEXISTENCE

REQUIRED:

- Manual .198 and relay candidates use different schemas, parsers and storage namespaces.
- A manual candidate never contributes to relay quorum.
- A relay candidate never overwrites or mutates the stored manual candidate.
- The selected website value always displays its source as manual or companion-relay.
- A valid manual candidate remains available when relay is no-quorum, conflicting, expired,
  revoked, deleted, withdrawn or unavailable.

PROPOSED precedence when both candidates are valid:

- A source is newer only when its entire source interval is strictly later than the other's.
- If relay is definitely newer, select relay.
- If manual is definitely newer, select manual.
- If intervals overlap, treat them as tied and select manual.

OPEN DECISION: Confirm this interval-based precedence. An alternative "relay whenever available"
policy is simpler, but it would not honor the agreed conservative tie rule.


14. PRIVACY SURFACE

The website receives and stores only this bounded masked aggregate. It must not receive the wider
Companion file or any of the following:

- character, member, Discord, GUID, BattleTag, account or contributor identifiers;
- names other than the eleven canonical guild names;
- witness totals, Council participation, agreement percentages or conflict partitions;
- ranks, notes, chat, keys, alt estimates, claims or raw observations;
- request JWS content or replay identifiers.

The relay may keep only the minimum internal provenance needed to deduplicate, recompute, revoke
and erase. Internal provenance is not a feed extension point.


15. RETENTION, REVOCATION AND ERASURE

REQUIRED behavior:

- Erasure or contributor revocation removes the contributor from active candidate sets and
  recomputes every affected metric.
- Any affected accepted result is replaced under a new sequence/ETag. If quorum is lost or conflict
  remains, no count is published.
- Person mappings, opaque identifiers or hashes, claims, raw inputs, snapshots, logs and backups
  each have a documented deletion rule.
- Retained raw data cannot recreate an erased account mapping or claim.
- A durable deletion ledger outlives the oldest backup and is reapplied before any restored backup
  becomes available.

PROPOSED maximum retention:

  active account/person mapping and verification claims:
    while active; delete from primary storage within 24 hours of a valid erasure request

  raw observations and raw checkpoint material:
    24 hours

  current and historical bounded masked snapshots, if history is needed:
    30 days

  redacted security and site-access logs:
    30 days

  encrypted backups:
    30 days

Logs never contain Authorization, compact JWS, account identifiers, raw observations or unmasked
counts. Deletion records must be applied on restore so a backup cannot repopulate erased claims.

OPEN DECISION: Confirm each duration, the erasure service-level target and whether any masked
snapshot history is needed at all.


16. VERSIONING

REQUIRED: v1 is an exact schema. Additive fields are not silently accepted. A shape or semantic
change ships as v2 with new fixtures.

PROPOSED: Keep v1 available for at least 90 days after v2, with Deprecation and Sunset headers.


17. NORMATIVE FIXTURE MATRIX

The separate fixture package must freeze and test at least:

- exact two-witness agreement;
- tolerance-based approximate agreement;
- Olympus II four-to-one acceptance at 80 percent;
- a single source with no public count;
- a two-to-two conflict with no public count or partitions;
- a nontransitive A-B-C chain that does not become one cluster;
- two characters from one linked account deduplicated to one witness;
- an unverified claim that cannot force an account merge;
- Council alone remaining no-quorum;
- Council plus one distinct ordinary witness following normal two-witness rules;
- character quorum with stale or insufficient online observations;
- independently corroborated online zero;
- small total, small online and complementary-remainder masking after aggregation;
- expiry, revocation, deletion and complete-snapshot disappearance;
- an explicit tombstone state;
- manual fallback after relay withdrawal;
- 304 preserving original source age, followed by an expiry transition with a new ETag;
- rounded relay and exact manual intervals overlapping and selecting manual on the tie;
- wrong scope, guild and faction;
- invalid or replayed JWS alg, kid, iss, aud, method, target, scope, expiry and jti.

The validator must recursively reject identity fields, witness-count fields, Council participation,
conflict partitions, unmasked small groups, unknown keys and noncanonical guild ordering in every
public expected result.

The reference validator checks fixture structure and the documented policy only. It does not and
must not claim to verify a production signature, real Ed25519 key handling, atomic jti consumption,
server storage, network behavior, the production aggregation implementation or addon runtime.


18. OPEN DECISIONS SUMMARY

The following must be answered before the fixture package becomes normative or any adapter is
wired:

1. Exact endpoint path and canonical query serialization.
2. Exact Forever PvE realm-group mapping and minimal native aliases.
3. Whether an authenticated but unverified account can ever be a qualifying witness.
4. Authoritative Council source, owner, expiry and revocation procedure.
5. Character and online tolerance constants.
6. Character and online freshness windows.
7. Even-sized cluster median: rounded middle pair or lower median.
8. Whether online publication additionally requires an accepted character total for masking.
9. Manual-versus-relay precedence for overlapping source intervals.
10. Retention durations, erasure service level and whether masked snapshot history is needed.
11. Endpoint rate limit and v1 deprecation period.

Until those items are frozen, this remains a review draft. Production activation, key exchange,
deployment and publication remain separate approvals.
